title: LLM for Public Data: Generating Synthetic Personas for Population Analysis
summary: This platform uses an LLM to generate statistically accurate synthetic personas from public data, allowing policy researchers and business strategists to model entire populations who are poorly represented in standard AI training data.
beneficiaries: Policy researchers, data scientists, and business strategists who need to understand, model, and serve populations (e.g., low-income or rural households) that are poorly represented in standard, web-based LLM training data.
geoScope: Global. It currently has U.S. data in the tool.
deploymentStage: Pilot / Limited Deployment: In use with a specific partner or limited user group.
aiModel: A proprietary model built on a Large Language Model (LLM) fine-tuned for querying and analyzing structured public datasets.
barriers: Primary barriers include: (1) Building trust with public sector and academic users who are accustomed to manual data extraction. (2) Sourcing and integrating the vast array of relevant international public datasets to expand the tool's geographic scope beyond the U.S.
enablers: A strategic partnership with a federal agency or a multinational body to serve as a pilot partner. This would provide access to key datasets and build the credibility needed for wider adoption.

title: AI generated video to bring oral history images & interviews to life
summary: This video uses AI video generation to bring Dorothea Lange's historic photos to life.
beneficiaries: This benefits anyone interested in the history of the forced internment of over 120,000 Japanese Americans during World War II.
geoScope: The video (by Giovanni Abitante) is public on YouTube.
deploymentStage: Broadly Deployed: Widely available and in active use.
evidence: It was a Runner up at the Metamorph AI Film Festival.
aiModel: The creator used Hailuo and Kling video generators and the voices in this film are real. They come from survivors, their families, and historians, collected through interviews and documentaries.
barriers: The main barrier is public opinion that puts all AI video generation into the category of "slop." This is an example of using AI video generation for social good.
enablers: There are already film festivals to promote AI video generation, and there could be more education in this area.

title: Smarter, greener mineral exploration using AI
summary: For exploration teams, regulators, and host communities, this AI technology fuses geology, geophysics, and remote-sensing data to pinpoint high-probability deposits—cutting guesswork, drilling, costs, and environmental disturbance.
beneficiaries: Communities living near prospective copper and lithium deposits—especially in the African Copperbelt—who face the greatest environmental disturbance from exploration.
geoScope: Zambia's Copperbelt (Mingomba project near Chililabombwe), with pilot studies in Québec and Australia—expanding globally.
deploymentStage: Pilot / Limited Deployment: In use with a specific partner or limited user group.
evidence: A Copperbelt exploration team using the AI platform re-ranked legacy targets with newly digitized 1950s-era maps; the system prioritized deeper structures that prior campaigns had overlooked, leading to the Mingomba drill hits and a faster path to mine planning—reducing unnecessary holes and footprint versus "grid-drill everything."
aiModel: A proprietary, multimodal AI system that combines rock/soil data and geophysical surveys with satellite and field photos to make a probability map of the best places to drill. It uses multiple models, shows how confident it is, and keeps learning from old maps and every new drill result in each region.
barriers: Fragmented data: Incomplete/uneven legacy maps and proprietary surveys limit training and transfer. Capital risk: High upfront cost for AI + new surveys with uncertain returns. Permitting & data rules: Slow approvals and data-sovereignty constraints impede sharing and validation.
enablers: Open up the maps and data. Governments and survey agencies should share old geology maps, drill results, and geophysics in easy-to-use, standard formats so AI tools can learn faster. Create joint funds (public + private) that help pay for early AI-guided surveys and drilling, in return for clear environmental reporting and benefits for local communities.

summary: The KOS employs a combination of methods to help prevent human-caused catastrophes.
beneficiaries: Organizations and the public exposed to preventable human-caused catastrophes.
deploymentStage: Research / In Development: A model or system being actively built or studied in a lab setting.
evidence: Described in company publications and case materials.

title: Library-augmented generation (LAG) for scholarly research
summary: An MCP server plus Claude integration lets AI query library holdings directly, yielding sources that are grounded in real collections and encouraging users to read and verify the works themselves.
beneficiaries: Scholars, students, and libraries seeking AI research assistance grounded in licensed and open collections rather than the open web.
geoScope: United States, with applicability to any library system.
deploymentStage: Pilot / Limited Deployment: In use with a specific partner or limited user group.
evidence: Early faculty demos describe the setup as a way to incorporate AI while preserving scholarly practices—relief that AI complements, not replaces, research. Queries are routed to library holdings with direct links (open and licensed), yielding "100% non-hallucinated" sources and encouraging users to read/verify the works themselves.
aiModel: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server + Claude plugin enables what the team calls "library-augmented generation" (LAG).
barriers: Wider use is slowed by content licenses and strict vendor rules, privacy laws that require careful handling of patron data, and security risks like prompt injection. It's also hard to connect the system to many library tools (catalogs, link resolvers, museum/archives systems). Costs add up for hosting, vector search, and API calls.
enablers: Open and vendor-neutral ways to connect LLMs to library and museum collections—simple, standard APIs and licenses that allow retrieval and linking without letting content be used to train models, with clear logs for accountability. Consortial funding to build a shared, open-source toolkit and run pilots across many libraries.

title: GrantRail & Adequacy AI for education finance
summary: An agentic AI system for faster grant decisions and equity-aligned education finance analytics.
beneficiaries: Education funders, local education agencies, and students in under-resourced districts.
deploymentStage: Research / In Development: A model or system being actively built or studied in a lab setting.
evidence: N/A but projected: 50% faster grant decisions; 30% lower diligence cost per learner; and 20% increase in placements into living wage or skill aligned opportunities.
aiModel: The GrantRail & Adequacy AI system uses a network of autonomous Omni Agents built on Airtable's AI infrastructure, integrated with large language models (GPT-5) for natural-language reasoning and policy analysis. Each agent runs specialized tasks such as funding adequacy detection, redistribution simulation, and stakeholder insight generation.
barriers: 1. Limited access to standardized, disaggregated education finance data across states. 2. Privacy and compliance concerns related to integrating public and school-level datasets. 3. Lack of trust in AI-generated policy recommendations without clear audit trails. 4. Resistance from entrenched education funding structures that prefer opaque budgeting methods. 5. Resource constraints among local education agencies to implement AI-assisted funding analytics.
enablers: 1. Integration partnerships with major funders and education networks (e.g., Stand Together, Walton Family Foundation, or Charter School Growth Fund) would provide real grant pipelines for the platform to analyze and optimize. 2. Access to open philanthropic and state education grant data would allow stronger ROI models, sustainability forecasting, and impact benchmarking across regions.

title: Provenance-aware, human-participatory data infrastructure
summary: ODL builds the data layer that model builders rely on: provenance infrastructure documenting the full lifecycle of training data, plus data measurement and valuation tools.
beneficiaries: Data contributors, model builders, and institutions trying to use data responsibly.
deploymentStage: Broadly Deployed: Widely available and in active use.
evidence: ODL-supported data networks have engaged over 1 million contributors, demonstrating that user-consented, provenance-tracked data can be collected at meaningful scale. ODL's research on data measurement and valuation provides tractable methods for identifying how different datasets influence model predictions.
aiModel: ODL does not build a single model; ODL builds the data layer that model builders rely on. This includes provenance infrastructure (systems that document the full lifecycle of training data) and data measurement & valuation tools (methods for estimating data influence on model behaviour).
barriers: Inconsistent data rights and portability laws create uncertainty for institutions trying to use data responsibly.
enablers: Partnerships with public institutions, civil society groups, and private companies to pilot provenance-aware, human-participatory data pipelines at scale.

title: VoteMate: AI-powered nonpartisan voter information
summary: An AI assistant giving voters fact-based, nonpartisan, and useful information for making informed decisions in elections.
beneficiaries: Voters across all 50 states seeking trustworthy ballot and election information.
deploymentStage: Pilot / Limited Deployment: In use with a specific partner or limited user group.
evidence: We have conducted a limited proof-of-concept supporting voters before and during the November 2025 elections. The beta ran from 10/2/2025 through 11/4/2025 and we served a total of 7,652 users in all 50 states + DC. Efforts were targeted in Virginia, New Jersey, New York, California, and Texas.
aiModel: For the beta, we deployed GPT-5 nano with a robust system instructions file which was designed, purpose-built, and extensively tested to shape the responses to fit the following criteria: fact-based, backed by verified sources, nonpartisan, unbiased, and useful specifically to voters making informed decisions. We also provided a grounding framework on voting and elections.
barriers: (1) Getting the word out through marketing and other efforts (2) Public skepticism and build trust (3) Some technical limitations around collecting nationwide ballot data, which we're working towards (4) some financial limitations, which we're actively fundraising to address
enablers: (1) Reliable funding from foundations, individuals, etc. (2) Additional volunteers to support our efforts, especially folks with technical skills. VoteMate is an all-volunteer run organization so far.
